newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady at 3.05/3.10, trade calm.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady at 3.05/3.10, trade calm.

text.p: German call money was steady on Tuesday, with dealers reporting rates trading between 3.05 and 3.10 percent in very quiet trade.
Dealers added, however, that the majority of what business there was, was concentrated at the lower end of that range.
With reserve levels coming back up after dipping earlier in the week, liquidity was reasonable and the market calm, they said.
Daily reserves held by commercial banks at the Bundesbank rose to 40.7 billion marks on Monday from 39.9 billion on Friday, while the monthly average was steady at 39.9 billion.
At its tender on Wednesday, the Bundesbank was expected to fully replace the expiring securities repurchase agreement of 61.0 billion marks, traders said.
Borrowing on the Lombard emergency facility was negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) was quoted at 3.08667 percent on Tuesday, slightly softer than Monday's 3.09633 percent.
